Serial constraints cleared: ⛔ **This card does NOT take the `sql-driver.ts` serial slot** — it lands in `schema-drift.ts`, a distinct file (verified by filename). The `sql-driver.ts` slot was freed when **PR #12714 (#12017) merged as `d29e42f8`**, and queued sibling **#12593** is the next claimant there — ⛔ not dispatched, so no collision either way. Neighbouring card **#11722** (an `applyMigrationEntries` reporting gap) is `pm:on-hold`, not in flight. No open PR touches `schema-drift.ts`.

### The defect — measured on `origin/main` at claim time, controls firing

The varchar differ's whole branch is gated on the author having declared a bound. Live at **`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts:833`** (⚠️ locate by **symbol** `declaredMaxLength`, ⛔ never by that line number):

```
declaredMaxLength !== undefined &&   // <-- the gate
```

Controls: `widen_varchar` / `narrow_varchar` → **6** hits in that file; `enforcesVarcharLength` → **3**; the file is present. The probe addresses real code.

⇒ On a **pre-existing** table, split by whether a bound was declared:

| declaration | physical column | drift says |
|---|---|---|
| `Field.signature({ maxLength: 4096 })` | `varchar(255)` | ✅ `widen_varchar`, with a remedy |
| `Field.signature()` — **no bound** | `varchar(255)` | ⛔ **nothing** — no number on the declared side to compare |

**The second row is the common case** — the card's own motivating example is a data-URI PNG written into a plain `signature`. After #11875/#12119 a **new** column is TEXT and correct; an existing deployment upgrading to that release sees **no change and no diagnostic**, and the server still refuses at `22001` / `ER_DATA_TOO_LONG` with nothing anywhere saying why the fix did not reach it.

⇒ Same `declared ≠ enforced` shape as the #11374 / #11431 / #11875 family, arriving one door further along — at the **migration** seam rather than the authoring or write seam.

### Section — TRIAGE'S ROUTE (⛔ measure-first; this is a route, not a ruling)

> **Inventory before remedy.** First enumerate how a deployment would even **learn** it has pre-existing `varchar(255)` `signature`/`qrcode` columns. Then choose.

- **The in-code fix**: a drift op keyed on **TEXT-family membership** rather than on a declared number. If it proves sound, it closes the declared≠enforced gap at the migration seam the way the authoring / write / storage seams are already closed.
- **Documenting the manual `os migrate` step**: ⛔ **this touches release-notes territory and therefore comes back as a REPORT, ⛔ never as a rider on `content/docs/releases/`.** That directory is release-owned; a code PR editing it is exactly what the guardrail stops.
- A one-off migration in the release carrying #11875 is the card's third candidate and has the same release-notes entanglement — same treatment.

### ⛔ What the card explicitly does NOT claim — do not manufacture these

- ⛔ **No claim that #12119 is wrong or incomplete.** It delivered all three seams the maintainer ruled, and declared this boundary honestly in its own changeset. ⛔ This is not a reason to revisit it.
- ⛔ **No frequency measured.** How many deployed tables actually carry such a column is **unknown** — which is precisely why triage put inventory first. ⛔ Do not assert a blast radius you have not measured.
- ⛔ **No opinion on the remedy** is on the card. The route above is triage's preference; a better one measured on the tree wins.

⛔ Confirm or refute every reading above on the current ref before writing code. `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a legitimate delivery.

### What "done" must show

A drift op that reports nothing is indistinguishable from no drift. Reproduce the **silence** first — a pre-existing `varchar(255)` column with an **undeclared** `signature`/`qrcode` field producing **zero** drift ops — then show the same case reported. Name a **positive control** proving the differ can emit an op at all in that same run (the declared-bound row above is the obvious one).
